short: Bottleneck target (M02) and auditory-spectrogram route (M06) are standard; gains rest on one speaker, a re-implemented baseline and a vocabulary-cued test on four seen GRID speakers.
position: Lip2AudSpec [@akbari2018lip2audspec] changes the training target (M02, a noisy 32-unit autoencoder bottleneck) and the acoustic route (M06, an 8 kHz auditory spectrogram with iterative inversion); both are standard. The bottleneck gain is shown on one speaker in one run, and four of five bottleneck settings score lower PESQ than direct spectrogram regression (Tables 7-8). The pitch and naturalness gains are not credited to the representation, because the baseline is a re-implementation with an unreported protocol and no ablation swaps the representation. On the same four GRID speakers later work reaches STOI 0.731 against 0.446 for Lip2AudSpec [@kefalas2023large; @vougioukas2019video], and on unseen speakers it produced no intelligible speech [@vougioukas2019video].
